Assembly Stdio

Editor, interpreter and debugger for IJVM and Intel 8088 assembly.

Getting started

  1. Select File > Change Working Path and pick the folder of your programs. Open shows only the files in this folder.
  2. Select File > New and create a .a8088 or an .ijvm file. The editor also opens .asm and .jas files.
  3. Copy an example program from Help > 8088 Instructions or Help > IJVM Instructions (section Esempi) into the file.
  4. Click Run to execute the program, or Debug to stop before the first instruction.

The output, the input and the messages appear in the terminal. The memory viewer shows the state of the program.

Window and menus

Window

  • The window has a custom frame on Windows, Linux and macOS. You can resize it from every edge.
  • On macOS, the window buttons are on the left, and the File and Help menus are in the macOS menu bar. On Windows, the maximize button shows the Snap Layouts.
  • The title shows the working directory. Double-click it to maximize or restore the window. Drag it to move the window.
  • Ctrl+click the title (Cmd+click on macOS) to open the working directory in the file browser.
  • Drag the border between the editor and the debugger to resize the two panels.
  • The app remembers the open files and the size of the window.

File and Help menus

  • Change Working Path: select or create the folder of your source files. Double-click a folder to select it.
  • Open: open a source file of the working directory. If the file is already open, its tab becomes active.
  • New: create a .a8088 or an .ijvm file and open it. The dialog asks before it replaces a file.
  • Save as...: save a copy of the current file with a new name, as a file of the same language. The copy does not open.
  • Help: this page, the 8088 instructions and the IJVM instructions.

Code editor

Editing

  • The syntax colors follow the file extension.
  • The autocompletion suggests the instructions and the words of the file after the first character.
  • The editor saves the file while you type, before each run, when you change tab and when you close the app.
  • Ctrl+X and Ctrl+C cut or copy the whole lines of the selection.
  • Ctrl+Shift+Up and Ctrl+Shift+Down move the selected lines.
  • Ctrl+D duplicates the line, Ctrl+Shift+L deletes it, and Ctrl+T swaps it with the line above.
  • Ctrl+F opens the search bar, with plain text or regular expressions. The search ignores the case.

Tabs and view

  • Each file has a tab. Drag a tab to move it. Turn the mouse wheel on the tab bar to scroll it.
  • The tabs that do not fit are in the overflow menu at the right of the tab bar.
  • Two files with the same name show their path from the working directory.
  • If a program outside the app changes a file, the tab loads the new text when you select it.
  • Zoom: Ctrl +, Ctrl -, Ctrl 0 or Ctrl + mouse wheel. Pinch on a macOS or Windows touchpad.
  • During a run, a green arrow and a green background mark the next line. The editor scrolls to it when the file of the program is in the selected tab.

Execution toolbar

ControlFunction
RunExecute the current file without pauses.
DebugStart the current file and stop before the first instruction.
StopEnd the program. The button shows only while a program runs.
Step 1 / Step 10In debug mode, execute 1 or 10 instructions.
Automatic steppingIn debug mode, pick an interval (500 ms, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 10 s) and click the metronome button. The program executes one instruction at each interval. Click the button again to stop.
HEX / DECShow the memory values in hexadecimal (default) or in decimal. A click changes every value at once.

Memory viewer

Header

  • The program counter, in decimal and in hexadecimal.
  • The next instruction and its line in the source file.
  • The current scope (method or label) and the language.
  • A light blue light runs around the header while the program waits for input.

Values

  • A new value flashes green, a changed value flashes blue and a removed value flashes red.
  • In debug mode, the viewer scrolls to each new value or frame.
  • The copy button of a value puts name: value on the clipboard, in the current base.
  • At the end of a run the viewer keeps the final state. The next run clears it.
LanguageContextContents
IJVMCONSTANTSThe constants of the .constant block.
IJVMSTACKOne frame for each method call. A frame shows its variables first, then its operand stack by word address. A called method is inside the frame of its caller.
8088REGISTERSAX, BX, CX, DX with their 8-bit halves, SI, DI, BP, SP and the segment registers DS, ES, SS.
8088STACKThe stack words by address. The words of a subroutine, from its return address down, are in a group with the label of the subroutine.
8088MEMORYThe bytes of the .DATA segment (from 0x1000) and of the .BSS segment (from 0x2000) that are not zero. Each cell is one byte. The bytes of a data label are in a group with the label and its address, for example msg (0x1000), and each cell has the name of its offset: msg+0, msg+1. A byte outside every label has its address as its name. The cells of the .DATA segment show before the first instruction, because the program loads them at the start.
8088FLAGSThe zero, carry, sign, overflow and parity flags.

Terminal

Output and messages

  • The program output is white and appears while the program runs. The text that you type is green.
  • Only the message tag has a color: [INFO] light blue, [WARNING] yellow, [EXCEPTION] red.
  • At the end of a run, the terminal shows the exit code, a separator and the prompt <path of the current file> >>.
  • You cannot change the earlier output.

Commands

  • Ctrl+F or the find button opens the search bar: regular expressions, previous and next match, and the match count.
  • Ctrl+L or Ctrl+Shift+K clears the terminal when the terminal has the focus. The right-click menu and the clear button of the terminal toolbar (click two times) also clear it.
  • The right-click menu also has Paste, Copy and Select All.
  • The toolbar buttons scroll to the top and to the bottom.
  • Zoom uses the same keys and gestures as the editor.

Program input

How to type an input
When the program executes IN (IJVM) or the _GETCHAR system call (8088), it waits, and the light runs around the memory viewer header. Type the characters in the terminal and press Enter.
RuleDetails
One character, one inputEach input instruction reads one character. The line 12; gives three inputs: '1', '2' and ';'. One line or three lines give the same result.
ValueThe program receives the character code, not the digit: '1' is 49 (0x31). Subtract 0x30 to get the digit.
Maximum value255 (0xFF). Each input is one byte, so each character must have a code from 0 to 255. The terminal does not send a line with another character and shows a warning.
EnterEnter sends the line. It does not send a newline character. An empty line sends nothing.
End of a numberThe course programs end a number with ; (0x3B). Type ; after the digits.
Typing aheadThe characters wait in a queue until the program reads them, up to 4096 characters.

Addresses

ItemIJVM8088
Program counterByte address in the method area. main starts at 0. Each other method follows in source order, after a header of 4 bytes (parameter count and variable count).Byte address in the text segment, from 0.
Instruction size1 byte. 2 bytes for BIPUSH, ILOAD, ISTORE. 3 bytes for GOTO, IFEQ, IFLT, IF_ICMPEQ, IINC, LDC_W, INVOKEVIRTUAL. Labels take no space.Opcode, ModR/M byte, displacement and immediate, as in the 8086. A jump uses the short form when its target is in range. The sizes are close to the real encoding but not exact.
StackWord addresses. The frame of main starts at 0x8000 with its variables. A called method uses the address of its OBJREF as its base (LV). The link pointer, the parameters, the variables, the saved PC and the saved LV come before its operand stack.Addresses in the stack segment, from 0xFFFF down. CALL pushes the byte address of the next instruction and RET jumps back to it.
Data-.DATA from 0x1000, .BSS from 0x2000.

Display limits

ItemLimit
Call frames (IJVM)The 16 most recent frames.
Stack entriesIJVM: the 64 most recent entries of each frame. 8088: the 64 most recent words in total.
Memory bytes (8088)The first 128 bytes that are not zero, by address.
Terminal output200,000 characters for each run. The terminal hides the rest and shows a notice.
